rows.grounds: bahuvrīhi compound referring to the aṇu endowed with karmic residue; analyzed as given, no internal split.
abstract noun marking the property of being a cause in this doctrinal context.
connective linking the preceding causal claim to the conditional clause.
optative/conditional form marking a doctrinally posited possibility rather than a stated fact.
locative of bhava marking the sphere of embodied existence for the aṇu.

items.question: On what doctrinal grounds must the aṇu endowed with karmic residue possess causal status within embodied existence rather than outside it?
premises: The aṇu is endowed with a stored karmic residue at the point of consideration.
Causal status is a property that must be assigned to that endowed aṇu.
That assignment of causal status is posited as holding specifically within embodied existence.
items.inference: For an aṇu endowed with karmic residue, the property of being a cause would hold in the sphere of embodied existence.
uncertainties: The precise scope of 'causal status' here is not determined by this verse alone.
It is undecidable from this verse whether the possibility is necessary or merely admissible.
items.plain_english: For one endowed with karmic residue, causal status would hold in embodied existence.

rows.grounds: Past-participle compound marking a conclusion established by reasoning, not by direct perception.
Negated pronoun used to exclude an alternative item from the set under consideration.
Refers to a distinct effect different from one already posited in the argument.
Clausal marker giving the intended meaning of the preceding reasoning as a whole.

items.question: By what reasoning-based exclusion must the posited causal status yield no distinct additional effect beyond what the argument already allows?
premises: The conclusion in question is established by reasoning rather than by assertion alone.
No other distinct effect is admitted as required by that reasoning.
The force of the argument is to be taken as that exclusion of an additional effect.
items.inference: What is established by reasoning is not the admission of another distinct effect, but the meaning given by that exclusion.
uncertainties: The identity of the effect already posited is not specified by this verse alone.
It is undecidable whether the exclusion is absolute or restricted to the present context.
items.plain_english: This is established by reasoning: there is no other distinct effect; that is the meaning.

rows.grounds: Fused form as given; marks afflictions appearing in varied and noble forms. Internal fusion noted, not split into rows.
Connective joining the forms of afflictions to the class of those affected.
Technical term for the kleśas in Śaiva Siddhānta, load-bearing and not reducible to a generic emotion.
Genitive plural describing those bound by attachment to objects, i.e. the class on whom those afflictions arise.

items.question: For those attached to objects, what kind of afflictions must arise in order for the previously posited causal relation to hold in embodied existence?
premises: Afflictions belong to the class of factors that arise for those attached to objects.
Those afflictions appear in varied and noble forms.
The presence of such forms is posited as a fact for that attached class.
items.inference: For those attached to objects, afflictions of varied and noble forms arise as part of the embodied situation under consideration.
uncertainties: The exact taxonomy of the forms is not enumerated by this verse alone.
It is undecidable from this verse whether all listed forms arise simultaneously or in different cases.
items.plain_english: And the afflictions of varied and noble forms arise for those attached to objects.

rows.grounds: Locative marking a different section of the present work, not a different text.
Future passive/impersonal future marking a promised demonstration within the work's own structure.
Clausal closure marking the end of the present argument unit.
Auspicious closure formula common to doctrinal verse units; here marks closure, not a new premise.

items.question: What constraint does a promise of demonstration in another section place on the completeness of the argument offered in verses 226 through 228?
premises: The present argument unit is being closed at this point.
A demonstration of what remains is promised in another section of the work.
The closure is marked as auspicious without adding a new doctrinal premise here.
items.inference: The account given so far is offered as sufficient for closure of this unit, with further demonstration deferred to another section.
uncertainties: The exact content to be shown later is not specified by this verse alone.
It is undecidable whether the deferral is for proof, for application, or for both.
items.plain_english: This will be shown in another section; thus, auspiciousness.
